label: Batched group prefill
mechanism: co-admitted prompts prefill as one right-padded length-sorted batched traversal — expert dequant amortized across rows
hypothesis: The accepted cycle is now PREFILL-term-dominated: exp-0013's accepted 89.7 tok/s block is 448 reqs / 639.5 s = 91.4 s per 64-cohort = ~61 s serial prefill (~67%) + ~30 s decode, because exp-0007..0013 rebuilt the decode step while every prefill still walks the 66 layers once PER SEQUENCE. Prefill is GPU-bound in the grouped packed-NVFP4 GEMM (exp-0009 profile: 93.4% of prefill CUDA pre-BLOCK_M-fix), whose per-(expert, n-tile, k-chunk, m-chunk) full-tile dequant is paid once per sequence: at T~736 only 17-24 rows/expert fill one BLOCK_M-32 m-chunk, so 64 serial walks pay ~64 full-matrix dequant passes per layer per cohort, each serving ~17 rows. Right-padding co-admitted prompts into ONE batched walk (the exp-0009 DEADENDS groundwork: admission groups under a 4 GiB padded-scores budget, per-row states seeded through the unchanged per-seq slice calls, causality isolating real rows from pads) raises rows/expert to ~G x 17 and pays the walk's Python once. Two refinements were forced by measurement: (a) unsorted FCFS packing wasted ~33% of all per-token work on pad rows (measured 1.19x) — stable LENGTH-SORTING the admits before packing (partition stays a pure function of the admitted lengths; running-list order untouched) recovers it; (b) an idle-edge 150 ms accumulation window in EngineLoop keeps a retiring cohort's replacement arrivals from fragmenting into tiny first groups. MEASURED (one resident load, N=64 canonical-ISL-class prompts 500..999, sorted groups [45,19]; t_prefill_batch_exp0014_sorted2 log): serial 75.9 s vs grouped 58.4 s = 1.30x on the prefill term; in-situ through the live server (exp0014_http_ab2 log): 1.15x at 32 concurrent (arrival-race fragmentation bounds it below the engine-level ceiling). NOT expected to reach the groundwork's 1.5-2x projection: exp-0009/0010 already cut the per-pass dequant cost the projection assumed, and attention's padded-score share grows with G. prefill_heavy is untouched by design: an 8K pair exceeds the scores budget (every group is a singleton -> bitwise the per-seq path) and at ~192 rows/expert its dequant is already amortized — the win is specific to short-ISL admission cohorts.
